ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening against OFAC's SDN List, the European Union Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, and the Spanish System of International Sanctions (BOE). All UBOs and authorized signatories are subject to enhanced due diligence pursuant to Articles 4, 14 and 15 of Ley 10/2010. The protocol includes an independent negative-news, PEP and royal-family linkage screen, a sworn PEP-status statement from every direct shareholder, and an ongoing transaction monitoring plan to be activated upon incorporation.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Mercantil Central (RMC) - online certification system; public or notary-led application also accepted through CIRCE (Centro de Información y Red de Creación de Empresas) platform.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be written in Spanish or in any co-official Spanish language (e.g., Catalan, Basque, Galician) and must be pronounceable and distinctive in the Spanish phonetic system. Foreign words may be accepted if they are commonly recognized or untranslatable, but must be transliterated into Latin script; all names must conform to commercial-registry practice (Reglamento del Registro Mercantil, articles 404-407).
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon a negative name decision, the applicant may (i) request written reconsideration before the RMC within 10 working days of notification; (ii) file a recurso de alzada with the Dirección General de Seguridad Jurídica y Fe Pública (Ministry of Justice) within one month; and (iii) after exhaustion of administrative remedies, bring a contentious-administrative action before the Audiencia Nacional. Parallel re-application with an alternative name is permitted without prejudice. The certificate validity is not offered for extension beyond 90 days.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual-address service is acceptable for the sole purpose of receiving official notifications at the SL's registered office, but it cannot satisfy the operational substance required for ISIC 3240 (laser cutting and 3D wooden puzzle assembly). Industry licensing, municipal activity permit, labor-safety inspection and AEAT substance controls require a physical workshop or industrial unit in Spain. Therefore, the proposed setup should combine a virtual address with a contracted physical production site, regardless of the limited scale of assembly.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High: 70-80% likelihood of unannounced on-site inspection in the first 24 months, owing to CO2 laser equipment, combustible-dust exposure, machinery safety duties, and worker exposure risks; inspections may be carried out by ITSS, local town-hall activity inspectors, and tax administration officials.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Real Decreto Legislativo 1/2010, de 2 de julio (Ley de Sociedades de Capital, LSC), Articles 4 (minimum capital), 20-22 (public deed of incorporation and mandatory contents), 28-31 and 33 (registration in the Mercantile Registry and acquisition of legal personality); Royal Decree 1784/1996 on the Mercantile Registry Regulation; Law 14/2013 on Support for Entrepreneurs (CIRCE electronic incorporation regime).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Mercantil Central (RMC) for the denomination certificate and the Registro Mercantil Provincial of the province where the registered office is located for the inscription, with mandatory notarial intervention by a Spanish Notary.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Escritura Pública de Constitución (Public Deed of Incorporation) granted before a Spanish notary and filed with the Registro Mercantil Provincial.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Mandatory minimum fully paid-up capital of EUR 3,000 (approximately USD 3,240) for the Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada under LSC Article 4. The amount must be fully subscribed and paid in cash at deed execution and deposited in a blocked account of a Spanish or EU credit institution in the name of the company in formation; the bank-issued capital deposit certificate (certificado de desembolso) is attached to the public deed. Funds may be disbursed only after the Mercantile Registry inscription.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, FIRST, that the share subscription described in the deed is ratified and the EUR 3,000 capital is fully paid up per the bank certificate; SECOND, that the registered office is fixed at [Registered Address], within the territorial jurisdiction of the [Provincial] Mercantile Registry, according to Article 2 of the Bylaws; THIRD, that [Full Name] is appointed Sole Administrator (Administrador Único) with full powers under the Bylaws, and [Full Name] is appointed Secretary; FOURTH, that the Administrator may apply for the NIF, open bank accounts, sign contracts, file industrial and environmental license applications, and perform all acts necessary to complete registration and commence operations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Reserve the Corporate Denomination (Negative Name Certificate)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Mercantil Central (RMC), online via the Sede Electrónica (www.rmc.es)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the denomination-reservation request through the RMC electronic portal, identifying the legal form (SL) and proposing up to three alternative names. The RMC verifies that no identical or strikingly similar company exists and issues the negative certificate (certificado negativo de denominación) within three business days. The certificate is downloadable in PDF and remains valid for three months, extendable for a further three months, during which the deed must be executed.
required_dossiers: RMC electronic application form for denomination certificate
Copy of DNI/NIE or passport for each founding member
Certificate of representation when the applicant acts on behalf of a shareholder
List of up to three proposed company names
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is denied for similarity, file a new application immediately with the alternative names; RMC issues the substitute certificate within one to two working days. If the certificate expires, renew the reservation before notarial execution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Open the Corporate Bank Account and Deposit Minimum Capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Spanish or EU credit institution authorized by the Banco de España
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a corporate account for the company in formation at the chosen bank, using the provisional denomination 'ES_SL Constitución SL in formation'. Deposit the full EUR 3,000 minimum capital and instruct the bank to block withdrawals until registration. Obtain the statutory certificate of deposit (certificado de desembolso) addressed to the notary, showing the corporate name in formation, the number of shares subscribed, and the amount deposited.
required_dossiers: Draft bylaws (estatutos) signed by the promoters
NIE and passport copies of the shareholders
Corporate resolutions and powers of attorney where a shareholder is a legal person
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requires enhanced due diligence, supply notarized corporate charters, shareholders registers, and bank references for entities; upon a bank refusal, use a second institution or deposit the capital with the notary in the form of a public deposit (consignación notarial) certified in the deed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execute the Public Deed of Incorporation Before a Notary
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notario of the notarial district where the registered office is located
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Present the name certificate, the capital deposit certificate, and the approved bylaws at the notarial appointment. All founding members, in person or by special proxy, declare their subscription, confirm payment, approve the corporate purpose covering precision CO2 laser cutting, 3D mechanical wooden puzzle assembly, and distribution, and adopt the First Board Resolution. The notary verifies legal capacity and form, calibrates the LSC requirements, and issues the certified first copy (primera copia) for registry filing.
required_dossiers: Negative denomination certificate valid at the date of execution
Official identity and tax residence documents of each member
Special power of attorney if representation is granted
Unofficial draft of the deed prepared by the notary
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary flags a defect (e.g., an invalid corporate purpose clause or inconsistent address), correct the bylaws by private written consent and re-execute the deed the same day or by deed amendment; do not exceed the validity of the name reservation.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) – Sede Electrónica (https://sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-owned Spanish Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada (SL) must first obtain a definitive NIF (Código de Identificación Fiscal, now Tax Identification Number for companies) by filing Form 036 or 037 with AEAT before commencing taxable activities. Non-resident directors or shareholders must obtain an NIE (Número de Identidad de Extranjero) and, if required, appoint a fiscal representative. VAT registration is integrated into the same Form 036/037 filing; no separate VAT ID number is issued, but the NIF serves as the Spanish VAT number. The application may be submitted electronically with a recognized digital certificate, via AEAT's Telematic Registry, or through a notary for company incorporation.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Spain does not provide a check-the-box classification regime for domestic limited liability entities; an SL is mandatorily treated as a separate corporate taxpayer under Corporate Income Tax (Impuesto sobre Sociedades). Available statutory elections include: the option under Article 65 of the Corporate Income Tax Act to pay current tax liabilities at the time of accrual, elections for consolidated tax grouping (Grupo Fiscal) under Chapter VI of the Consolidated Tax Regime (a group headed by a Spanish resident entity may elect the special consolidated regime), and, for transactions falling under domestic anti-hybrid rules, elections allowed under Law 27/2014 Art. 15.bis to align treatment with EU Anti-Tax Avoidance Directive (ATAD). Additionally, instalment payment methods (whether under the 'base, facturación, or part of corporate tax quota') may be elected on Form 036.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Impuesto sobre el Valor Añadido, IVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general registration threshold is applicable; any person carrying out taxable supplies in a business capacity must apply for NIF/VAT registration (Form 036/037) prior to commencement. For intra-EU distance sales of goods to consumers in Spain, an annual threshold of EUR 10,000 (excluding VAT) applies, above which registration in Spain is required. For the simplified VAT regime, turnover ceilings of EUR 150,000 for total supplies and EUR 50,000 for purchases/imports are applicable to eligible small businesses.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: As implemented under the then-named 'Crea y Crece' Law (Law 9/2021) and the Anti-Fraud Law (Law 11/2021), operators must issue electronic invoices and maintain invoicing software with integrity and auditability, eventually mandating QR / verifiable electronic invoicing for B2B transactions (expected B2B e-invoicing obligations start between 2026 and 2027). Large enterprises (business volume above EUR 8,000,000) and VAT groups are subject to the Immediate Supply of Information (SII / Suministro Inmediato de Información) system, which requires near-real-time reporting of all invoicing records to AEAT via an API (web services) in XML format, with strict deadlines: 4 days from issuance of invoices (or 8 days for certain records). Digital stamping is a future obligation; currently, SII uses authorised software to transmit records; non-SII taxpayers must submit periodic VAT returns through AEAT's electronic registry but no fiscal clearance/mandatory digital stamp is applied in general.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Supplies of goods transported to non-EU destinations (exports) are taxed at 0% VAT in Spain (exemption with credit) when: (i) the seller proves that the goods left Spain and the EU within the legally required period (generally within 90 days or 3 months for certain transport); (ii) the buyer is non-EU; and (iii) transport or dispatch outside the EU is evidenced by a customs export declaration lodged with the Spanish customs authorities by the exporter (or if export is made from another Member State, from that MS). For services linked to exported goods, e.g. transport services directly related to export, the 0% rate applies when the services are directly linked to the physical movement of the goods to a destination outside the EU. Offshore services to non-EU clients are generally subject to the place-of-supply rule: if the customer is a taxable person outside the EU, supply of such services is outside the scope of Spanish VAT (0% effect), requiring documentary proof of customer status and business location.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (DEX / Export Customs Declaration) lodged via the Spanish electronic customs system (DUA / SGL)
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill (or other equivalent transport document) evidencing physical departure of goods from the EU
Inward Remittance Certificate (bank transfer / SWIFT payment evidence) showing settlement under the applicable FX rules
Proof of delivery/acceptance by the foreign consignee
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Export zero-ratings are highly scrutinised by AEAT; missing or inconsistent proof triggers immediate rectification and recovery of unpaid VAT, plus late payment interest. Under Article 84 of the General Tax Law (Ley 58/2003), fraudulent or negligent export claims are subject to penalties ranging from 50% to 150% of the misclaimed VAT amounts. Criminal liability may arise under the Spanish Criminal Code for aggravated tax fraud in excess of EUR 120,000. AEAT may retroactively assess within the standard four-year limitation period; where falsified documents are used, the limitation period extends to ten years, with full clawback and interest.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de España (Bank of Spain), with SEPBLAC serving as the AML/CFT supervisory unit within the Bank of Spain; the Comisión de Inversiones Exteriores (Foreign Investment Commission) and AEAT (Spanish Tax Agency) handle related reporting and tax validation.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Spain operates under the fully liberalised capital and current account convertibility provisions of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union (Articles 63–66) and Royal Decree 304/2014 on external transactions. There are no exchange controls, forced conversion requirements, or pre-approval mechanisms for the movement of capital, dividends, trade profits, or loan repayments by non-residents. Profit remittance is unrestricted in EUR, though dividends paid to non-residents are subject to Non-Resident Income Tax (IRNR) withholding at the domestic treaty rate (e.g., 19% for non-residents, 0%–5% under most EU/Andean treatment and tax treaty provisions) and must be supported by corporate resolutions and Form 216/240 filings. Transactions with non-residents exceeding the Banco de España reporting threshold (currently €50,000 per transaction or annual cumulative equivalent) must be filed using Form E (Declaración de Operaciones con No Residentes).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Spain imposes no mandatory surrender or minimum conversion ratio for export proceeds. Export receipts may be freely held in foreign currency in Spanish or EU bank accounts, converted to EUR, or applied to operational disbursements. The only applicable requirements are (i) commercial documentation retention for VAT and corporate income tax purposes, (ii) invoicing and foreign currency valuation under Spanish GAAP, and (iii) Form E reporting to Banco de España when the transaction exceeds the €50,000 threshold. No statutory strict deadline exists for converting export receipts; however, the accrual basis of tax accounting requires recognition at the year-end exchange rate and enforcement of payment terms via standard commercial collection channels.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account and Operational Account
Capital Escrow Account and Operational Account
Capital Escrow Account and Operational Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: High feasibility as an ancillary EUR-IBAN treasury layer using EU/EEA passported electronic money institutions (e.g., Wise Business, Revolut Business, Qonto) licensed in another EU jurisdiction and operating under the Revised EMD/PSD2 in Spain. These EMIs are legally viable for low-risk commercial transactions, VAT payments, and cross-border receivables, but they cannot serve as the sole principal account for the Spanish SL because Spanish notaries require a domestic bank certificate for capital contribution validation (certificación bancaria de desembolso), and tier-1 banks are generally required for commercial letter of credit origination, direct debit mandates, and participation in official financing programmes (ICO). For Amazon and Stripe settlement, an EMI can function as a collection account; nevertheless, a Banco de España-addressable Spanish IBAN bank account remains mandatory for statutory corporate, tax, and insolvency requirements. Regulatory caution: the Spain AML authorities (SEPBLAC) expect robust customer due diligence and may reject EMI-only banking structures for newly convened non-resident-owned SLs without a local physical banking footprint.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Spanish tier-1 commercial banks generally mandate a physical appearance of the sole administrator or a duly authorised representative at a local branch for initial account opening. Remote opening is technically permissible under Law 10/2010 (AML prevention), but banks rarely extend this to non-resident directors owning a Spanish SL without an pre-existing relationship. The standard process requires a personal appointment in Spain, or if remote is exceptionally granted, a notarised video call with certified ID, plus delivery of the signed appointment documents. The non-resident director must hold a valid NIE (Número de Identificación de Extranjero), provide a foreign tax identification number, and attend (in person or through a Spanish resident representative/power-of-attorney holder) the capital deposit confirmation with the notary. All corporate documents (public deed of incorporation, NIF certificate, power of attorney, passport copies) must be valid, apostilled (Hague Convention) where applicable, and translated into Spanish by a sworn translator if necessary.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO is tax-resident outside the EU/EEA (e.g., Latin America, Asia) with no verifiable local source of funds.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified copy of passport and NIE; current tax residence certificate (Certificado de Residencia Fiscal) issued by the home tax authority; sworn translation of residence proof; bank references from a licensed foreign bank for the prior 12 months; CV and business overview; explanation of the Spanish SL economic nexus (local warehouse, Amazon fulfilment, target EU market); the investment amount and source-of-wealth statement; audited or notarially verified financial statements of the transferor entity, if applicable.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The Spanish entity is newly incorporated with no local payroll or fixed operating premises.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Lease agreement for the Spanish operational premises or third-party logistics contract (warehouse/smart storage); payroll declarations and Social Security (TGSS) registrations for local staff; evidence of registration with the Spanish Almacenista or seller registration if operating via Amazon; bank account invoice trail from initial operating activities; demonstration of an actual order-to-cash cycle with invoices and delivery documentation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The intended operational function is perceived as a booking/agency shell rather than a genuine manufacturing/trading company.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Production equipment invoices (CO2 laser cutter, edge sanders), supplier contracts for raw MDF/wood panels, energy usage statements, product safety conformity certificates (CE), commercial contracts with customers/sellers, and factory-visit or photographic/VAT inspection records proving the physical transformation of goods.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Third-party settlement concentration through Amazon Pay and Stripe, causing commingling of sales receipts across entities or unexplained refund/dispute patterns.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Separate e-commerce seller account contracts naming the Spanish SL as the contracting party; platform consolidated payout reports; Stripe/Amazon Pay settlement logs; refund and dispute rationales; VAT returns (Modelo 303/390); and AEO/export documentation if goods are warehoused and sold cross-border.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Capital injection exceeds Spain-documented lawful salary or undistributed profits of the non-resident shareholder.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarially certified shareholder resolution approving capital increase; bank debit confirmation from the originating shareholder account; withholding tax clearance certificate from the shareholder's tax residence; commercial loan agreement or family gift deed if the injection is structured as debt; evidence of prior payment of gift/inheritance tax where applicable; a signed source-of-funds declaration aligned to the amount in the bank reference.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: All inbound non-resident capital injections must be routed through formal banking channels using a SWIFT MT103 payment in EUR (or USD/EUR asset transfer) with the mandatory payment purpose description 'Suscripción de capital social' and the notary file reference. The Spanish bank will report the transaction under Banco de España Form E using the foreign investment reporting classification for direct portfolio/investment capital, generally code 701 (foreign direct investment in Spanish companies). Upon credit to the Spanish SL's escrowed capital account, the bank must provide a certificación bancaria de desembolso confirming receipt of funds to the notary for the capital contribution verification before execution of the public deed. If the capital injection exceeds €50,000, the company must file the Form E with Banco de España within the statutory reporting window (normally 30 calendar days of the transaction). Timely bank credit confirmation, FX spot conversion if funds arrive in USD, and retention of the MT103 and bank receipt are mandatory for tax deductibility of interest if debt is later capitalised.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For EU suppliers (wood panels, packaging, laser parts), disbursements use SEPA Credit Transfer (SEPA) through the same Spanish bank or an EMI, with immediate MSCI/FIBAN clearing in EUR. For non-EU suppliers (e.g., Chinese laser machinery, coatings), standard clearing rails are SWIFT MT103 for international commercial payments under terms of sales, with full attachment of the proforma/commercial invoice and customs entry declaration for the Banco de España Form E report if exceeding the €50,000 threshold. Larger capital equipment purchases may use a confirmed irrevocable commercial letter of credit (LC) at sight pursuant to UCP600, typically issued through Banco Santander, BBVA, or CaixaBank, with transaction preference to use a Chinese/Asian advising bank using the Telex or SWIFT MT700 structure. Documentary collections (D/P) and trade open-account solutions are available for repeat suppliers. All outgoing wires require a signed bank mandate and KYC-verified UBO; payments to high-risk jurisdictions may require additional sanctions screening and statement of end use.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: FX forward contracts (EUR/USD, EUR/CNY, EUR/GBP) for projected operational cash flows
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for currencies with local currency restrictions only if the counterparty bank confirms a valid spot restriction underlying and the hedge is non-speculative
Cross-currency swaps (FX swaps/CCS) for term-matching of material asset and liability positions
OTC EUR/USD European plain-vanilla options (with EMIR trade-reporting obligations if the Spanish SL exceeds clearing thresholds)
Short-dated FX options combined with forwards (zero-cost collars) for total hedging cost reduction

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Deposit of Annual Accounts (Depósito de Cuentas Anuales)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registro Mercantil (Commercial Registry of the registered office)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Shareholders' meeting must approve the annual accounts within six months of fiscal year-end (calendar year: by 30 June); deposit at the Commercial Registry within one month of approval (calendar year: by 30 July)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Registry closure (cierre registral) preventing any further filings until accounts are deposited; administrative fines under Article 379 LSC ranging EUR 1,200 to EUR 60,000; possible automatic liquidation if a company files persistently no accounts for several years

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate Income Tax Return (Impuesto sobre Sociedades - Form 200)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 25 days following the six-month post-year-end period; for a calendar tax year ending 31 December, the filing deadline is 25 July
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing surcharges of 5% (within 3 months), 10% (within 6 months), 15% (within 12 months) or 20% after 12 months, plus late-payment interest and potential penalties up to 150% of the due amount; no administrative strike-off

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Audit is mandatory if the SL meets at least two of the following three thresholds for two consecutive years: (i) total assets exceed EUR 4,000,000; (ii) annual net turnover exceeds EUR 8,000,000; (iii) average number of employees exceeds 50. Audit also required if requested by shareholders holding at least 5% of the capital or where legally mandated due to public subsidies or other regulatory reasons.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Spanish General Chart of Accounts (Plan General Contable) applicable to individual accounts; simplified PYME framework may be used if turnover is less than EUR 10,000,000; IFRS only required for consolidated groups or specific regulated entities, not for this standard SL.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Spanish law does not require a separate annual UBO confirmation filing; beneficial ownership information must be filed with the Commercial Registry upon incorporation and updated within 30 days of any change in ultimate beneficial ownership. The SL must maintain its share register (Libro Registro de Socios) and permanently document shareholding transfers, recording the identity of the transferee, especially where UBO data changes.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (Libro Registro de Socios)
Minute Book (Libro de Actas - shareholder and, if applicable, board meetings)
Accounting Ledgers (Libro Diario and Libro de Inventarios y Cuentas Anuales)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% general corporate income tax rate for Spanish resident companies, including an SL.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Newly created entities generally qualify for a 15% rate during the first profitable tax period and the immediately following period, subject to statutory exclusions. For tax periods beginning in 2025, entities with prior-year net turnover below EUR 1 million generally apply 21% to the first EUR 50,000 of taxable profit and 22% to the remainder; qualifying entities with turnover below EUR 10 million generally apply 24%. These reduced rates are subject to transitional rules and eligibility conditions. Qualifying research and development, technological innovation, audiovisual production, and certain employment incentives may reduce the effective rate through tax credits. The patent-box regime can provide a 60% reduction of qualifying net income from qualifying intellectual property. Spain does not generally provide a blanket corporate tax holiday for ordinary manufacturing or toy businesses.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Indefinite. Spanish tax losses generally carry forward without a fixed expiration period, subject to annual utilization limits, ownership-change anti-abuse rules, minimum taxation rules, and applicable tax-group restrictions.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Modelo 200, Impuesto sobre Sociedades e Impuesto sobre la Renta de no Residentes, declaration for resident companies. Filed electronically through the Spanish Tax Agency (AEAT) electronic office using the Sede Electrónica de la AEAT.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Filed within the 25 calendar days following the six months after the end of the tax period. For a calendar-year taxpayer closing on 31 December, the normal filing window is 1 July through 25 July of the following year. If the last day is not a business day, the applicable electronic filing rule extends the deadline to the next business day.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter the SL's NIF, legal name, tax domicile, tax period start and end dates, entity classification, accounting period, and filing type.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident shareholder is not entered as the taxpayer unless it carries on business through a Spanish permanent establishment. The Spanish SL files using its own Spanish NIF.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter the profit or loss per statutory accounts before corporate tax and reconcile it to the Spanish tax base.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Exclude the non-resident parent's accounting results. Include only the SL's Spanish accounts and properly recorded transactions with non-resident related parties.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report permanent and temporary adjustments, including non-deductible expenses, depreciation differences, provisions, impairment, exempt income, participation exemptions, and other book-to-tax differences.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply Spanish deductibility, documentation, arm's-length, interest limitation, anti-hybrid, and anti-abuse rules to cross-border charges.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Identify available prior-year tax losses and the amount utilized in the current period, subject to the applicable percentage limitations and minimum taxable-income rules.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Losses of a foreign shareholder or foreign affiliate cannot be used by the SL unless transferred under a legally applicable Spanish tax-consolidation or restructuring regime.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Claim eligible R&D, technological innovation, audiovisual, double-taxation, employment, and other statutory credits with supporting documentation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign tax credits require qualifying foreign tax, income inclusion, statutory limits, and documentary evidence. Do not claim a treaty benefit as a domestic tax credit without satisfying the relevant requirements.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Tax rate and gross corporate tax
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Apply the general, newly created entity, micro-enterprise, or other applicable rate to the adjusted taxable base.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The residence or nationality of the shareholder does not itself change the SL's corporate income tax rate.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Payments on account and withholding credits
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Credit Modelo 202 advance payments, Spanish withholding suffered, and other permitted prepayments against final corporate tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Do not credit withholding suffered by the foreign shareholder against the SL's corporate tax return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Tax payable, refund, or balance carried forward
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Calculate the final amount payable or refundable and provide the authorized direct-debit or payment reference details.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The payment account must comply with AEAT payment and direct-debit requirements. The foreign parent remains separately responsible for any shareholder-level withholding.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Provide the required balance-sheet, profit-and-loss, tax reconciliation, related-party, participation, loss, and other annex information required by Modelo 200.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose material related-party transactions, cross-border financing, royalties, management services, and shareholder transactions consistently with statutory accounts and transfer-pricing records.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Voluntary late filing without prior AEAT notice generally gives rise to a surcharge of 1% plus 1% for each completed month of delay up to 12 months; after 12 months, the surcharge is generally 15% plus late-payment interest. The surcharge may be reduced by 25% if statutory payment conditions are met. Filing after an AEAT notice, failure to file, or inaccurate filing may produce penalties generally ranging from 50% to 150% of the unpaid tax, subject to statutory minimums, aggravating factors, and voluntary-compliance rules.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Modelo 202, corporate income tax payments on account, filed electronically through the AEAT Sede Electrónica.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Quarterly payment windows, normally in April, October, and December.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Generally filed and paid during the first 20 calendar days of April, October, and December. For the December installment, the relevant period is normally 1 December through 20 December. Entities required to use the net-tax-base method may have a different calculation basis and must observe the same statutory filing windows.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter the SL's NIF, name, tax period, installment number, and applicable corporate-tax return period.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the Spanish SL's identification details. A foreign parent is not the filer unless it has a Spanish permanent establishment subject to the payment-on-account regime.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Calculate the installment using either the prior year's final corporate tax liability or, where mandatory or elected, the current-period tax base method.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include cross-border transactions only to the extent they affect the Spanish taxpayer's current Spanish tax base.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Apply the statutory percentage and deduct permitted payments or credits to determine the installment payable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Do not reduce the Spanish installment by anticipated foreign-parent tax or by unverified treaty relief.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Submit the payment reference or authorized direct-debit instruction through the AEAT system.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Confirm that the payment account and authorization are accepted by AEAT before the deadline.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late voluntary payment generally attracts the statutory surcharge regime for late self-assessment payment, plus interest where applicable. Failure following an AEAT notice or an incorrect payment-on-account calculation may trigger tax penalties and interest.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Modelo 232, information return on related-party transactions and transactions or situations involving countries or territories classified as tax havens or non-cooperative jurisdictions, filed electronically through the AEAT Sede Electrónica.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual, where the statutory reporting thresholds or relevant jurisdictional conditions are met.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Generally filed during the month following the ten-month period after the end of the tax period. For a 31 December year-end, the normal deadline is 30 November of the following year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Identify the related person or entity, relationship category, transaction type, aggregate value, and valuation method.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report qualifying transactions with the foreign parent, affiliates, directors, and other related persons using consistent legal names, tax identifiers, currencies, and transfer-pricing records.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report transactions that exceed the applicable aggregate or transaction-type thresholds, including financing, royalties, services, goods, and transfers of assets.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Aggregate transactions by related counterparty and type where required; retain reconciliations to the general ledger, invoices, contracts, and Local File.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Disclose transactions or holdings covered by the applicable Spanish non-cooperative-jurisdiction rules.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Perform jurisdiction classification using the current Spanish list and applicable anti-abuse provisions rather than relying solely on an old treaty or OECD list.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Incorrect, incomplete, or omitted information may trigger specific information-return penalties, generally calculated by item or data omitted, subject to statutory minimums and maximums. Additional corporate tax adjustments and transfer-pricing penalties may apply.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 19% Spanish withholding tax generally applies to dividends and other profit distributions paid by a Spanish SL to a non-resident. The EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive exemption may apply where the recipient is a qualifying EU or EEA parent, holds at least 10% of the Spanish subsidiary, satisfies the minimum holding-period requirement or provides the required commitment, and the arrangement is not abusive. Treaty rates may reduce the rate, commonly to 5% or 10%, depending on the applicable treaty and ownership conditions.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Before payment, obtain a valid certificate of tax residence from the recipient's foreign tax authority and verify beneficial ownership, treaty residence, limitation-on-benefits or anti-abuse requirements, ownership percentage, holding period, and substance. Apply the reduced rate only where Spanish domestic law or the applicable treaty permits source-country relief and the payer can support the position. The Spanish payer must retain the residence certificate, ownership evidence, corporate resolutions, payment records, and beneficial-owner analysis. If relief is unavailable at source, withhold at the domestic rate and require the recipient to seek a refund from AEAT using the applicable non-resident tax refund procedure. Residence certificates should be current under AEAT practice and refreshed when required.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: The general Spanish domestic withholding rate for non-resident royalties and interest is generally 24%, subject to statutory exclusions and special regimes. The EU Interest and Royalties Directive may provide an exemption for qualifying associated EU companies that satisfy minimum ownership, holding-period, residence, subject-to-tax, and anti-abuse conditions. Applicable tax treaties commonly reduce royalty withholding to approximately 5% to 10% and interest withholding to 0% to 10%, but the exact rate depends on the treaty, beneficial ownership, permanent-establishment provisions, and anti-abuse rules. Payments to related parties in non-cooperative jurisdictions require enhanced review and may be denied treaty relief.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 250,000 aggregate annual value for transactions of the same type and under the same tax treatment with the same related person or entity is the principal exemption threshold from standard related-party documentation, subject to exclusions and transaction-specific rules. A Local File is generally required when the statutory documentation conditions are met. A Master File is generally required for Spanish entities belonging to a group with net turnover of at least EUR 45 million, subject to statutory exceptions. Country-by-country reporting generally applies to qualifying multinational groups with consolidated revenue of at least EUR 750 million.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Spain does not operate a single standalone regime titled Economic Substance Regulations equivalent to certain other jurisdictions. Substance is nevertheless assessed under the General Anti-Avoidance Rule, conflict-in-the-application rules, beneficial-ownership principles, anti-abuse provisions, controlled foreign company rules, EU parent-subsidiary and interest-and-royalty anti-abuse rules, and permanent-establishment doctrine. The SL should maintain real Spanish functions, personnel or outsourced operational capacity, premises or production capability where appropriate, decision-making, commercial risk, inventory and logistics records, bank-account control, accounting records, and evidence that intra-group services and financing provide a genuine benefit. Artificial arrangements lacking business purpose may be recharacterized, denied treaty or directive relief, or reassessed.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Corporate income tax evasion and fraudulent accounting
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Concealing sales, maintaining parallel accounts, fabricating expenses, using false invoices, deliberately understating inventory or profit, or claiming unsupported tax credits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative tax penalties can generally range from 50% to 150% of the unpaid tax, with interest and recovery costs. Serious tax fraud exceeding the criminal threshold may constitute a criminal tax offense, generally punishable by imprisonment and fines; aggravated cases carry higher imprisonment exposure and professional or public-contracting disqualification.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and de facto managers may incur criminal liability where they knowingly participate, civil liability for tax and creditor losses, and subsidiary liability under Spanish tax-law rules for culpable failure to ensure compliance. Travel restrictions or passport measures are not automatic and require judicial or statutory proceedings. Imprisonment is possible only where criminal elements and judicial conviction are established.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: False invoicing, VAT fraud, and carousel-fraud indicators
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Issuing or accepting invoices for services not supplied, misrepresenting intra-EU goods, manipulating VAT evidence, or using shell counterparties to obtain deductions or refunds.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: VAT reassessment, repayment of improperly claimed amounts, late-payment interest, and administrative penalties may apply. Deliberate large-scale fraud may result in criminal prosecution, imprisonment, fines, confiscation, and commercial disqualification.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who authorize or knowingly tolerate fictitious invoicing may face personal criminal and civil exposure. Corporate limited liability does not protect intentional fraud or participation in criminal conduct.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Charging non-arm's-length management fees, royalties, financing costs, or goods prices; failing to maintain contemporaneous documentation; omitting related-party transactions; or shifting profit without corresponding functions and risks.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: AEAT may make a primary adjustment, impose secondary adjustments, deny deductions, apply withholding consequences, and impose specific transfer-pricing documentation penalties. Documentation-related penalties can be assessed per missing, inaccurate, or incomplete data, subject to statutory limits; tax-adjustment penalties may also apply.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face civil or administrative liability where the breach results from culpable conduct or deliberate concealment. Personal criminal exposure generally requires intentional participation in tax fraud rather than a mere good-faith pricing disagreement.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Undocumented profit repatriation and withholding-tax failure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying dividends, interest, royalties, or service fees without withholding, applying treaty relief without a valid residence certificate, misidentifying the beneficial owner, or disguising distributions as deductible expenses or loans.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The SL may be assessed for the unpaid withholding, late-payment interest, and withholding-agent penalties. The recipient may lose treaty or directive relief, and the payment may be nondeductible or recharacterized as a distribution.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may incur subsidiary tax liability where they culpably fail to ensure withholding and payment. Deliberate concealment, false documentation, or sham loans may create criminal tax or commercial fraud exposure.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell company, sham substance, and treaty abuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using an entity with no genuine commercial function to obtain reduced withholding, route royalties or interest, conceal the ultimate beneficial owner, or book profits disconnected from personnel, assets, functions, and risks.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: AEAT may deny treaty or EU directive relief, apply domestic withholding, recharacterize transactions, impose tax and interest, and apply anti-abuse penalties. The General Anti-Avoidance Rule may permit reassessment of artificial arrangements.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and beneficial owners may face civil, tax, AML, and potentially criminal liability if they knowingly facilitate sham transactions or conceal ownership. Travel bans are not automatic and require a competent authority or court order.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting unexplained cash or crypto proceeds, failing to identify the ultimate beneficial owner, ignoring suspicious payment patterns, structuring transactions to avoid controls, or failing to maintain required customer and transaction records.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Spanish AML authorities may impose administrative fines, publicize serious sanctions, restrict management functions, and require remediation. Criminal money-laundering conduct may result in imprisonment, fines, and confiscation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Managers and directors responsible for AML controls may face personal administrative or criminal liability for knowing participation, grossly negligent facilitation, or obstruction. Corporate form does not shield personal criminal conduct.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Undeclared permanent establishment or foreign-controlled activity
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Allowing a non-resident parent to conduct regular sales, contract conclusion, inventory, installation, or dependent-agent activity in Spain without appropriate registration, accounting, tax filing, and withholding analysis.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: AEAT may assert Spanish permanent-establishment profits, corporate income tax, VAT, payroll obligations, withholding, interest, and penalties for failure to register or file.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face subsidiary liability for knowingly operating an undeclared taxable presence or obstructing tax collection. Criminal exposure requires deliberate and sufficiently serious tax fraud.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to maintain reliable books, destroying records, making unlawful distributions, paying related parties while insolvent, preferring insiders, or continuing operations while knowingly worsening creditor losses.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Potential consequences include rejected deductions, tax penalties, director disqualification, clawback of unlawful distributions, insolvency liability, damages, and criminal sanctions for accounting or insolvency offenses.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be ordered to restore assets, compensate creditors, return unlawful distributions, or cover insolvency shortfalls where statutory conditions are met. Imprisonment and travel restrictions require applicable criminal or judicial proceedings and are not automatic.
